  `user_options` is a first-class template field and that the configuration is written to
  `model_configuration_for_run.yaml`; that is how the mechanism was understood before this node
  existed. It was not enough: neither model already in the project could exercise it — route A's
  declares eighteen options that never arrive, route B's declares none — so "MLproject models are
  configurable" rested on reading code rather than on a model receiving a value. This node exists
  to replace that inference with a file.
  **Taking the model's own printed configuration as the evidence.** `train.py` prints the dict it
  receives, which was the first plan, and CHAP does not forward a subprocess's stdout at default
  verbosity, so nothing was captured. `model_configuration_for_run.yaml` is better evidence
  anyway: it is what CHAP wrote for the model rather than what the model says about it.
  **Widely separated alpha values rather than a fine sweep.** The question is whether a value
  arrives and does something, not what the best value is. 1e-5, 1e2 and 1e5 span five orders of
  magnitude, so an effect cannot be confused with noise — and this model is deterministic, so
  there is no noise floor to clear.
  **Running CHAP's own example shape, knowing it would probably fail.** Kept deliberately: a
  failure that halts the run and names its cause is the comparison that matters against route A,
  where the same class of disagreement produces a complete evaluation from a configuration that
  was never applied. Reporting only the three that worked would have hidden the more useful
  half of the finding.
  **No configuration is selected.** As in batch 8b, the plan's §3 forbids choosing between
  configurations on Lao scores. The alphas are a delivery test, not a search.
agency: `human-set` (that this repository is tried as a third case); `agent-autonomous` (the
  design, the values, and the decision to keep the failing run)

## Appended 2026-09-23 — re-run outside the repository, and the digests that changed

The first attempt copied the model into `results/model_copy` and ran it there. CHAP runs an
MLproject model by copying the directory into `runs/<timestamp>/` and building a `uv`
environment inside it, so each run left roughly 800 MB of the model's dependencies under a
results directory — including scipy's PNG test fixtures, which `/validate invariants` reported
as two dozen figures with no plotted values and no plotting script. It was right to. The script
now runs the model in a temporary directory outside the repository and keeps only the evidence.

Every result below was produced by that re-run. The four cases and their outcomes are unchanged.
